# TITLE LINUX SECURITY HANDBOOK # SUBTITLE 14. SELINUX AND APPARMOR # BADGES PAGE 14 OF 20 # SECTION_HEADINGS - MANDATORY ACCESS CONTROL - SELINUX MODES - ENFORCING, PERMISSIVE, AND DISABLED - SELINUX CONTEXTS - POLICY VIOLATIONS - GETENFORCE - SESTATUS - APPARMOR PROFILES - ENFORCE VERSUS COMPLAIN MODE - TROUBLESHOOTING BLOCKED APPLICATIONS SAFELY # BODY_PARAGRAPHS **MANDATORY ACCESS CONTROL** SELinux and AppArmor are Mandatory Access Control (MAC) systems that restrict what processes can do, even if they are compromised or running as root. **SELINUX MODES** SELinux operates in three main modes that determine how policies are enforced. **ENFORCING, PERMISSIVE, AND DISABLED** - Enforcing: Policies are active and violations are blocked. - Permissive: Policies are active but violations are only logged. - Disabled: SELinux is turned off (not recommended). **SELINUX CONTEXTS** SELinux uses security contexts (labels) to define what users, roles, types, and levels a process or file has. Contexts control access decisions. **POLICY VIOLATIONS** When a process is blocked by SELinux, an AVC (Access Vector Cache) denial is logged. These logs show what was blocked and why. **GETENFORCE** getenforce shows the current SELinux mode. Command: getenforce Example output: Enforcing | Permissive | Disabled **SESTATUS** sestatus displays SELinux status, mode, policy type, and other important details. Command: sestatus **APPARMOR PROFILES** AppArmor uses profiles to restrict programs. Each profile defines what the program can access. Profiles are stored in /etc/apparmor.d/ **ENFORCE VERSUS COMPLAIN MODE** - Enforce: Violations are blocked. - Complain: Violations are logged but not blocked. Use complain mode to test profiles before enforcing. **TROUBLESHOOTING BLOCKED APPLICATIONS SAFELY** - Review AVC logs: ausearch -m avc -ts recent - Identify the blocked action and target. - Adjust the policy or profile. - Use permissive or complain mode during troubleshooting. - Return to Enforcing/Enforce mode after validation. # IMPORTANT_FILES - **/etc/apparmor.d/**: Stores AppArmor profiles that define program access restrictions. # TABLES | Topic | Description | | :--- | :--- | | **MANDATORY ACCESS CONTROL** | SELinux and AppArmor are Mandatory Access Control (MAC) systems that restrict what processes can do, even if they are compromised or running as root. | | **SELINUX MODES** | SELinux operates in three main modes that determine how policies are enforced. | | **ENFORCING, PERMISSIVE, AND DISABLED** | • Enforcing: Policies are active and violations are blocked.
• Permissive: Policies are active but violations are only logged.
• Disabled: SELinux is turned off (not recommended). | | **SELINUX CONTEXTS** | SELinux uses security contexts (labels) to define what users, roles, types, and levels a process or file has. Contexts control access decisions. | | **POLICY VIOLATIONS** | When a process is blocked by SELinux, an AVC (Access Vector Cache) denial is logged. These logs show what was blocked and why. | | **GETENFORCE** | getenforce shows the current SELinux mode.
Command: getenforce
Example output: Enforcing \| Permissive \| Disabled | | **SESTATUS** | sestatus displays SELinux status, mode, policy type, and other important details.
Command: sestatus | | **APPARMOR PROFILES** | AppArmor uses profiles to restrict programs. Each profile defines what the program can access. Profiles are stored in /etc/apparmor.d/ | | **ENFORCE VERSUS COMPLAIN MODE** | • Enforce: Violations are blocked.
• Complain: Violations are logged but not blocked.
Use complain mode to test profiles before enforcing. | | **TROUBLESHOOTING BLOCKED APPLICATIONS SAFELY** | • Review AVC logs: ausearch -m avc -ts recent
• Identify the blocked action and target.
• Adjust the policy or profile.
• Use permissive or complain mode during troubleshooting.
• Return to Enforcing/Enforce mode after validation. | # COMMANDS 1. **getenforce** * Description: Shows the current SELinux mode. * Example output: Enforcing | Permissive | Disabled 2. **sestatus** * Description: Displays SELinux status, mode, policy type, and other important details. 3. **ausearch -m avc -ts recent** * Description: Reviews AVC logs for recent security events. # TIPS_NOTES_WARNINGS *Note:* "Disabled" mode for SELinux is not recommended. # PRACTICAL_EXERCISES *(None listed on this page)* # FOOTER_TEXT VERIQTA YouTube @veriqta GitHub @veriqta LinkedIn @veriqta X @veriqta Instagram @veriqta Telegram @veriqta # PAGE_NUMBER PAGE 14 OF 20
